concepts.def: Marshall (1890): satisfaction from consuming one more unit; diminishes as consumption rises, generating downward demand curve.
Change in real income from a price change alters quantity demanded; usually reinforces substitution effect.
Cheaper good substituted for relatively dearer ones; produces inverse price-quantity relationship.
Inferior good for which demand rises as price rises due to dominant income effect; rare in practice.
Luxury whose demand rises with price due to status signalling; Veblen (1899) 'conspicuous consumption'.
Difference between price received and minimum price producers would accept; area above supply, below price.
